SR.PP.V.TEKCHAND  THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 05.06.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

--------------------------------
 Dated this the 5th day of June 2024  ORDER
The petitioners are the accused in Crime No.189 of 2024 registered at the Vagamon Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 498A,323,325,354 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The crime is registered at the instance of the defacto complainant who is none other than the wife of the first petitioner.
The second and the third petitioners are the father and mother of the first petitioner.

According to the defacto complainant, the petitioners had physically and mentally harassed her between 09/04/2024 and 10/04/2024 and in the process, the first petitioner beat on the face of the defacto complainant resulting in rupture of left ear drum.

It is also alleged that, after her marriage with the first petitioner on 07/06/2020, while the defacto complainant was residing in matrimonial home, on 17/09/2020, the second petitioner, caught hold her from behind and when indecent act was reported to the third petitioner, she stated that such incidents are usual in all families.
2.
Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the allegations are cooked up and motivated by the matrimonial disputes between the first petitioner and the defacto complainant.
It is submitted that, the delay of more than three years in alleging misbehaviour by the second petitioner itself proves the falsity of such allegation.
Moreover, as against the third petitioner, who is recuperating after a surgery, no specific allegation is made.

3. Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that, the wound certificate of the defacto complainant reveals that she had blood clot in the left ear on 10/04/2024 and the possibility of the defacto complainant's eardrum being ruptured is also indicated in the certificate.
It is contended that, since there is clear cut evidence of the defacto complainant having been subjected to physical assault on 09/04/2024, the bail application is liable to be dismissed.
4. In the light of the observation in the wound certificate, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the first petitioner, against whom the specific overt act is alleged.

As far as the allegations against the second petitioner are concerned, there is substance in the submission of the learned Counsel that the inordinate delay in raising such a serious allegation casts doubt regarding its veracity.

5. Based on the above discussion, the Bail Application is disposed as under ;
The prayer for anticipatory bail made by the first petitioner is rejected.

If the first petitioner surrenders before the Investigating Officer within two weeks, he shall be interrogated and in the event of his arrest, produced before the jurisdictional Magistrate on the date of surrender itself.
On such production, the first petitioner may move an application for bail with notice to the Public Prosecutor concerned.
If so, the learned Magistrate shall consider the bail application and pass orders thereon, preferably on the same day.
